text: In 1964, a man flew from London to Australia... inside a wooden box.
Reg Spiers, a javelin thrower, was stuck in England. Broke. And his daughter's birthday was coming up back home.
But Reg worked in airport cargo, where crates flew around the world every day.
So he had a very bad, very brilliant idea.
His friend John built a box. Straps inside. A lid that opened from within.
Inside: a pillow, a torch, tinned food, and two bottles. One for water. One for... not water.
The label: a made-up customer in Perth, cash on delivery. John nailed it shut. Reg was now cargo.
Mid-flight, Reg sneaked out into the dark hold to stretch, and dived back in before landing.
In Bombay, the crate sat on the blazing tarmac. Upside down.
Inside, an oven. Reg stripped off his clothes and tried not to pass out.
Finally, Perth. Handlers swore about the size of the box. He didn't make a sound.
Then he got out of the crate, put on his suit, and made his way out of the airport unnoticed.
Sixty-three hours after London, he was in Perth. He hitchhiked to Adelaide, in time for the birthday.
Back in London, John got worried and called a newspaper. The story went worldwide.
Scared? Reg just shrugged: What was there to be frightened of?
